title: MCP servers not connected in -p (non-interactive) mode

triage_metadata.reasoning: No source files were pruned; all PR modifications directly address the reported issue.

summary.problem: MCP servers configured in settings are not available in non-interactive (-p / headless) mode because tool authorization rules for configured MCP servers are not automatically registered.
summary.root_cause: The policy engine builder `createPolicyEngineConfig` lacked logic to add auto-allow rules for configured MCP servers in headless mode, and `PolicySettings` in `packages/core/src/policy/types.ts` did not support an explicit `autoAllowInHeadless` setting for headless auto-approval.
summary.context: Headless CLI execution requires pre-approved tool policy rules to enable MCP tools without interactive prompts, while maintaining security by requiring an explicit setting (`mcp.autoAllowInHeadless`).

steps: In `packages/core/src/policy/types.ts`, extend the `PolicySettings` interface by adding an optional boolean property `autoAllowInHeadless` to the `mcp` object type definition.

In `packages/core/src/policy/config.ts`, inside `createPolicyEngineConfig`, add a check for non-interactive mode (`!interactive`), `settings.mcp?.autoAllowInHeadless`, and defined `settings.mcpServers`.

Iterate over `Object.keys(settings.mcpServers)` and skip any server already present in `settings.mcp.allowed`, covered by wildcard `'*'` in `settings.mcp.allowed`, or marked as `trust: true` in `settings.mcpServers[serverName]`.

For each non-duplicate server, push a policy rule to `rules` with `decision: PolicyDecision.ALLOW`, `priority: ALLOWED_MCP_SERVER_PRIORITY`, `source: 'Settings (Headless MCP Auto-Allow)'`, `modes: nonPlanModes`, `mcpName: serverName`, and `toolName` set to `${MCP_TOOL_PREFIX}*` if `serverName === '*'` or `${MCP_TOOL_PREFIX}${serverName}_*` otherwise.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When `autoAllowInHeadless` is enabled in non-interactive mode, configured MCP servers are granted allow policy rules automatically unless already explicitly allowed or trusted. In interactive mode or when `autoAllowInHeadless` is false, no auto-allow rules are created.
verification_steps: Run `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/policy/config.test.ts` to execute unit tests.
Verify unit test checking that `createPolicyEngineConfig` in non-interactive mode does NOT automatically allow configured MCP servers by default when `autoAllowInHeadless` is not set.
Verify unit test checking that with `autoAllowInHeadless: true` in non-interactive mode, allow rules are generated for configured MCP servers with source 'Settings (Headless MCP Auto-Allow)'.
Verify unit test checking that `autoAllowInHeadless: true` does not generate allow rules when `interactive` is true.
Verify unit test checking that duplicate allow rules are skipped if an MCP server is already in `mcp.allowed`, covered by `'*'`, or has `trust: true`.
